Title: Dreamland

Dreamland is an intimate look into life within a U.S. Army outpost during the chaotic period leading up to the Iraq War. Directed by Ian Olds and Garrett Scott, this documentary captures the daily lives of soldiers stationed at Camp Volturno, just outside Fallujah, in February 2004.

The camp was affectionately known among its inhabitants as "Camp Dreamland" due to its isolated location. Inside, the soldiers lived amidst constant tension and danger, facing not only combat situations but also the brutal realities of war.

The film features candid interviews with American soldiers recounting their experiences, along with dramatic scenes showing them patrolling through the volatile city of Fallujah. Interviews were conducted with local residents who provided a stark contrast to the soldier’s perspective, highlighting the impact of conflict on all sides.

Garrett Scott, the director, tragically lost his life to a heart attack at the young age of 37, just two days after the film premiered. This untimely death underscores the intense emotional weight and urgency behind the raw material captured in Dreamland.
